div.head: V Atr 1.1
div.ab: ⁊ ures hlafordes gerædnes ⁊ his witena is, þæt man rihte laga up arǽre ⁊ ælce unlaga georne afylle, ⁊ þæt man læte beon æghwylcne man rihtes wyrþe,
⁊ witena gerædnes is, þæt man rihte laga up arære ⁊ ælce unlaga georne afylle, ⁊ þæt man læte beon æghwylcne man rihtes wyrðe,
⁊ ure hlafordes gerædnes ⁊ his witena is, þæt man rihte lage up arære ⁊ ælce unlage georne afille, ⁊ þæt man læte æghwilcne man beon rihtes wurðe,
⁊ ure[s] hlafordes gerædnes ⁊ his witena is, þæt man rihte lage up arære ⁊ ælce unlage georne afille, ⁊ þæt man læte æghwilcne man beon rihtes wurðe,
And ures hlafordes gerædnes and his witena is þæt man rihte laga up arære and ælce unlaga georne afylle, and þæt man læte beon æghwylcne man rihtes wyrþe.

Und Verordnung unseres Herrn [Königs] und seiner Witan ist, dass man echte Rechtsordnungen (-nung D) aufrichte und jeden Rechtsmissbrauch eifrig abschaffe, und dass man jeden Menschen [seines] Rechtes theilhaftig sein lasse,
And it is the ordinance of our lord [the king] and his witan that just laws (law, D) be set up and every abuse of law be eagerly suppressed, and that every man be allowed to have his rights,
And the decree of our lord and of his councillors is, that justice shall be promoted and all injustice zealously suppressed, and that every man shall be allowed the benefit of the law,
And it is the decree of our lord and his councillors that just practices be established and all illegal practices abolished, and that every man is to be permitted the benefit of law;
And the decree of our lord and his councilors is that just laws be upheld and each injustice zealously eradicated, and that each person be afforded their legal rights.
div.note: G2 throughout omits ‘ures hlafordes … ⁊ his’ (‘our lord's … and his’). Liebermann compares III Eg 1.

Vgl.: ure Gescyppendes Blickling Homil. 11, 29.—Die Erwähnung des Königs bleibt hier und noch viermal in Variante fort: offenbar nicht bloss um zu kürzen; s. o. Einl. 13, auch zur Form der Königsbezeichnung

Cf.: ure Gescyppendes Blickling Homil. 11, 29.—The mention of the king is left out here and four more times in a variant: evidently not merely for the sake of brevity; see above Introduction 13, also on the form of the king's title
Folgendes unlaga ist wegen ælce Sg., also vielleicht auch laga, da im 11. Jh. acc. fm. sg. -a für -e vorkommt; s. o. Wb II 48 Sp. 3. Es ist zunächst an ungeschriebene Satzung gedacht

The following unlaga is sg. because of ælce, and so perhaps laga is too, since in the 11th cent. acc. fm. sg. -a occurs for -e; see above Wb II 48 col. 3. What is meant in the first place is unwritten ordinance
‘Unrecht’ Schmid zu allgemein. Solche Ordnungswidrigkeiten zählt Schreiber D 32, 1—5 auf
‘wrong’ (Schmid) is too general. Scribe D lists such irregularities in 32, 1—5
